case.background: A fixed amount of air is trapped above mercury in a sealed J-tube. Add mercury pressure while holding the thermal condition fixed, then infer how pressure and air volume are related.
initial_observations: Adding mercury compresses the trapped air reversibly.
The bath prevents deliberate temperature changes during a run.

controls.description: Condition of the surrounding bath during compression.
controls.name: thermal_condition

instruments.description: A sealed J-tube with trapped air, mercury, and pressure and volume scales.
instruments.name: sealed_j_tube

notes: The trapped amount of air and its temperature remain fixed.
Any non-empty subset of the two listed readouts may be requested.

FinalSubmission.model must equal 'expression'. FinalSubmission.parameters must equal {'outputs': {READOUT: EXPR, ...}} with exactly these readouts: air_volume_ml, absolute_pressure_kpa. EXPR is the shared family-neutral JSON arithmetic tree over public controls. Supported operators are: add, subtract, multiply, divide, power, negate, exp, log, sin, maximum, step. No candidate law family or truth-specific parameter slots are supplied.

readouts.description: Volume of the trapped air column.
readouts.name: air_volume_ml

readouts.description: Absolute pressure of the trapped air.
readouts.name: absolute_pressure_kpa

experiment.intent: Measure equilibrium volume and absolute pressure over a range of added mercury pressures to test P*V constancy versus a shifted inverse relation.

hypotheses.statement: At fixed temperature, the trapped air obeys Boyle's law: absolute pressure is inversely proportional to volume, P*V = constant.
At fixed temperature, the trapped air follows a shifted inverse relation P = a/(V-b), with b nonzero due to apparatus or nonideal effects.
